candidates.name: Cordon
candidates.pitch: A cordon lets movement through only at sanctioned points—AI actions cross only when a human waves them on.

candidates.name: Gnomon
candidates.pitch: An architectural term for precision and oversight, offering the sobriety and weight required for enterprise buyers.

candidates.name: Certes
candidates.pitch: Medieval certainty; archaic gravitas suggesting verified, trustworthy AI action under human sanction.

candidates.name: Hadrian Labs
candidates.pitch: Evokes the Roman boundary wall, signaling strict limits and a controlled architecture of distrust.

candidates.name: Billet Labs
candidates.pitch: Military quarters assigned strictly by warrant, capturing constrained agency, compartmentalized access, and disciplined, no-nonsense UK engineering.

candidates.name: AegisVector
candidates.pitch: Aegis implies protection, vector signals directionality; together they convey AI that moves only where authorised.

candidates.name: NovaPulse AI Solutions
candidates.pitch: A modern, innovative name that conveys energy and cutting-edge AI solutions for business.

candidates.name: Aegis
candidates.pitch: Classical shield; connotes protection through careful permission-gating and bounded agent autonomy.

candidates.name: Sovereign Air
candidates.pitch: Evoking 'air gaps' and supreme authority, it signals absolute operational boundaries, strict oversight, and elite British enterprise gravitas.

candidates.name: Sentinel
candidates.pitch: Watchful guardian; evokes controlled oversight and the architecture of distrust at your core.

candidates.name: Cautia
candidates.pitch: Derived from “cautious”, a concise coined word evoking measured AI trust, fitting mid‑market enterprise seriousness.

candidates.name: Veto Labs
candidates.pitch: A wry nod to the human-in-the-loop, ensuring risky AI actions require explicit human approval.

candidates.name: Corbel
candidates.pitch: An architectural stone bracket supporting massive weight only through structural restraint, embodying an unyielding, deliberate architecture of distrust.

candidates.name: Vouchsafe Labs
candidates.pitch: A deliberately old-fashioned promise of permission and protection, capturing governed AI that earns trust rather than assuming it.

candidates.name: Countermand Labs
candidates.pitch: Countermand means revoking an order, capturing the human power to stop risky AI actions before they proceed.

candidates.name: Imprimatur Labs
candidates.pitch: Imprimatur means official approval, fitting a firm where risky AI actions wait for human sign-off.

candidates.name: Seneschal
candidates.pitch: A seneschal held a lord's keys but never his throne—our agents act only with delegated, revocable authority.

candidates.name: Redoubt
candidates.pitch: A fortified refuge with clear defensive boundaries, evoking agents contained by design and consequential actions held behind approval.

candidates.name: Auctra
candidates.pitch: A coined blend of authority and strata, suggesting carefully layered powers, controls, and accountability for enterprise AI.

candidates.name: VeritasGate Labs
candidates.pitch: Latin for truth gate, signalling controlled AI flow and human‑approved decisions, a sober, weighty brand.

candidates.name: Chancery
candidates.pitch: Like a chancery court, every sensitive action is sealed, recorded, and released only once duly authorised.

candidates.name: Bailiwick Labs
candidates.pitch: Bailiwick means one's rightful domain, fitting AI agents confined to approved capabilities and information boundaries.

candidates.name: Penstock Labs
candidates.pitch: The sluice-gate that meters a river — Penstock fits an architecture admitting capability and information only where, and when, they should.

candidates.name: Claustra Labs
candidates.pitch: Latin for barred gates and grates—the physical architecture of 'information flows only where it may,' rendered sober and weighty.

candidates.name: Runnymede Labs
candidates.pitch: At Runnymede, power accepted limits; AI agents should act only within granted boundaries.

candidates.name: Chary Labs
candidates.pitch: Chary means cautiously reluctant—exactly the posture of least-privilege agents, mandatory approval gates, and need-to-know data flows.

candidates.name: Anchorite Labs
candidates.pitch: The medieval anchorite was walled into a cell by choice — wry, weighty shorthand for capability held strictly to its granted bounds.

candidates.name: Barbican
candidates.pitch: A medieval fortress guarding the gates — fitting for a firm channelling AI capability and data only where they should flow.

candidates.name: Seneschal Labs
candidates.pitch: A seneschal stewards power under strict instruction; our agents act only when explicitly granted.

candidates.name: Provost Labs
candidates.pitch: A provost governs by consent and check; AI agents should hold only delegated authority.

candidates.name: Vallum Labs
candidates.pitch: The Roman frontier system: ramparts, ditches, and controlled gates enforcing sovereign boundaries—architecture of distrust made imperial infrastructure.

dossier.C01: Companies House: blocked (THE CORDON LTD (14990561, active)). Free domains: none of .com/.co.uk/.ai/.io. Meaning: A cordon is a protective line of guards or barriers enclosing an area, from French "cordon" (cord/ribbon). Existing uses: Cordon (by Codezero), a 2026 free tool securing credentials across AI coding agents; Cordon AI (cordon-ai.com), an AI-native multi-model security validation platform; a separate "Cordon" security proxy enforcing policy/audit for AI agent-to-MCP tool calls; CORDONIQ (video conferencing security). Associations: "Cordon sanitaire": a barrier against disease or a political metaphor for isolating a party; mildly exclusionary connotation.
dossier.C02: Companies House: blocked. Free domains: none of .com/.co.uk/.ai/.io. Meaning: A gnomon is the raised part of a sundial that casts the shadow indicating time (also an L-shaped figure in geometry). Existing uses: Gnomon School of Visual Effects, a well-known VFX/games college in North Hollywood; Gnomon Digital, an AI/MLOps consultancy with clients incl. Société Générale and AXA; open-source "Gnomon" guardrails tool for AI coding agents; Gnomon-MCP, a maths/date tool for AI models. Associations: The sundial meaning is obscure to most; overlaps with an established, unrelated VFX education brand.
dossier.C03: Companies House: blocked (CERTES LIMITED (05129618, active)). Free domains: none of .com/.co.uk/.ai/.io. Meaning: Archaic English adverb meaning "certainly, in truth", from Old French, ultimately Latin "certus". Existing uses: Certes Networks, a Pittsburgh network-encryption/data-protection company (founded 2000) serving US federal and defence agencies, rebranded as Certes.ai for cybersecurity and data protection. Associations: Archaic word largely unknown in modern English; risk of mispronunciation or being read as a coined word.

Meaning: Named for Hadrian, Roman emperor (117-138 AD), best known for Hadrian's Wall across northern Britain. Existing uses: Hadrian (hadrian.io), an Amsterdam-founded (2021) agentic-AI offensive-security and attack-surface-management platform, recognised by Gartner and GigaOm, well funded and an active competitor in AI security. Associations: Hadrian's Wall (a barrier) and Roman imperial conquest; close overlap with the security company above.
dossier.C05: Companies House: blocked (BILLET LABS LTD (14310095, active)). Free domains: billetlabs.ai, billetlabs.io. Meaning: A billet is lodging assigned to a soldier, or a bar of metal ("machined from billet"); the latter is the common current usage. Existing uses: Billet Labs (billetlabs.com), an existing London company (founded 2022, Companies House 14310095) making CNC-machined PC-cooling hardware; a direct UK name clash in a different industry. Associations: "Billet" is everyday jargon in machining, car tuning and PC modding, so the name reads as hardware.

Existing uses: "Project Aegis Vector", a niche GitHub testbed for LLM/RAG vulnerabilities (not a company); otherwise shares the crowded Aegis namespace. Associations: "Attack vector" is security jargon; the compound can read as a generic, machine-generated brand.

cases.C27: Anchorite Labs is distinctive rather than generic: its chosen enclosure neatly signals bounded agency; “Labs” makes the monastic wit practical, with clear UK registration and usable domains.
cases.C16: Imprimatur signals rigorous sign-off, not censorship; UK Companies House and all key domains are clear, unlike vague 'shield' rivals.
cases.C18: Redoubt's defensive imagery nails contained-agent architecture; domain gaps and niche associations are solvable branding issues, not fatal flaws.
cases.C29: Palantir proved literary archaisms work; 'Seneschal' perfectly embodies our delegated-authority thesis, while pristine domain availability and Companies House clearance outweigh minor spelling hurdles with regulated, enterprise buyers.
cases.C23: Penstock Labs precisely evokes metered, controlled flow—capability and information passing only when granted. The Pentera sound-alike risk is limited; Companies House is clear, domains are available, and its sober engineering metaphor suits CISO buyers.
cases.C22: Labs separates it from Bailiwick.com; jurisdictional authority is exactly the governance story. Jersey/Guernsey tint is faint beside a precise, CISO-legible architecture metaphor.
cases.C15: Military tone? Zero-trust itself descends from military command doctrine. 'Countermand' names the exact human veto your architecture sells—instantly memorable, unambiguously ownable, sober where CISOs measure sobriety.
cases.C11: Distinct spelling, unrelated sector from funded Cautio. Latin 'cautio' means legal guarantee, richer than mere caution. Pronounce COH-shee-ah; .co.uk and .io free, Companies House clear.
cases.C25: Runnymede Trust is a think tank, not a tech firm; "Labs" signals product R&D. Magna Carta metaphor is exact for "architecture of distrust": agents granted limited, documented authority under rule of law. UK gravitas reassures
cases.C17: No core TLDs free, but .app/.dev/.tech available; precise medieval term for delegated, revocable authority mirrors thesis perfectly. Obscurity avoids AI clichés; pronunciation settles instantly. Tiny US consultancies pose zero market confusion.
cases.C26: Chary Labs perfectly mirrors the core ‘least‑privilege’ stance: ‘chary’ literally means cautious, signalling deliberate gate‑keeping. The name is unique, domain‑available, and avoids any existing AI‑security trademarks.
cases.C31: Vallum Labs invokes fortified boundaries—ramparts and controlled gates—directly resonating with the architecture of distrust. Despite a few nearby uses, the name remains distinctive and domain‑ready.
cases.C24: The architectural weight of Claustra pivots the risk of 'claustrophobia' into a promise of airtight control—precisely the rigorous boundary-setting demanded by CISOs in regulated sectors.
cases.C30: The institutional gravity is a strategic asset; it signals the governance, maturity, and delegated authority necessary to gain trust from enterprise CFOs and COOs in regulated markets.
cases.C12: Veto.so precedent is real but operates in different market (runtime auth for agents vs. enterprise AI workflows). Memorable, Latin-grounded, perfectly captures human override. Domain availability strong.
cases.C14: Vouchsafe.id is biometric identity; this is AI governance—distinct enough. Archaic language is intentional differentiator for serious buyers. Domains available. Harder to say is feature, not bug, for gravitas.

cases.C16: “Imprimatur” makes human approval the brand promise: weighty, memorable and apt for regulated buyers. Its ecclesiastical origin adds gravitas, while “Labs” keeps it technological; existing uses are adjacent, not identical.
cases.C30: Provost Labs signals governance by consent, not command—exactly the delegated-authority story CISOs want; academic tone reads as trustworthy, careful, and all domains are free.
cases.C18: Redoubt evokes contained, fortified agents with actions held behind walls until approved—precise architectural fit; Companies House is clear, meaning outweighs niche associations.
cases.C24: Rather than unsettling, the architectural Latin root provides precise, sober authority for gatekeeping; it offers completely clear UK registration, every key domain, and avoids crowded, generic security tropes entirely.
cases.C11: Evoking Roman legal guarantees (*cautio*), it delivers serious enterprise restraint. Clear of UK registrations, it uniquely targets enterprise AI workflows, distinct from India-focused hardware fleet dashcams.
cases.C23: Penstock Labs: sluice-gate precision—capability and information flow only when opened. Companies House clear, exact domains free; no Penstock Labs. Pentera soundalike is minor, category distinct.
cases.C27: Anchorite's chosen enclosure is the point: agents bounded by granted capabilities, not hermits shunning clients. Labs signals enterprise R&D; clear UK registration and usable .co.uk/.ai domains outweigh dormant US LLC.
cases.C14: Vouchsafe Labs can register full .com; vouchsafe.id is biometric identity, not governed AI. Archaic promise suits CISO trust; pronunciation is clear.
cases.C15: Militaristic? Yes—and that's the point. In defence, countermand is the disciplined word for revoking an order, fitting an architecture where AI holds only granted power. Sober, ownable, all domains free, no collisions.
cases.C31: Vallum.ai is a startup, not a fortress; co-existence with one early-stage rival is recoverable. The Roman frontier metaphor precisely encodes architecture-of-distrust—gates, ramparts, sovereignty—better than any generic shield name.
cases.C12: veto.so targets developers building agents; Veto Labs sells fixed-price consultancy to CFOs/CISOs in regulated UK enterprise. Different buyer, layer, and GTM. .ai/.io/.co.uk are standard for AI infra; the name perfectly embodies the architecture of distrust.
cases.C29: Pronounced SEN-uh-shal; spelling is phonetic. Archaic gravitas cuts through 'Shield/Guard' noise, signaling sober stewardship for regulated sectors. Exact .com secured. The medieval steward metaphor maps precisely to delegated, bounded agent authority.
cases.C25: Strong Magna Carta symbolism signals bounded AI authority, resonating with C‑level risk managers. Unique UK heritage, no tech conflict, and clear domain availability outweigh minor council/charity overlap.
cases.C22: The jurisdiction metaphor perfectly aligns with restricted AI capabilities. The offshore association suggests high-finance precision, while 'Labs' grounds the brand in technical rigor, neutralizing any perceived frivolity.
cases.C17: The steward metaphor is the definitive expression of delegated authority. Its rarity provides a sophisticated, singular identity that avoids AI clichés, turning obscurity into a mark of prestige.
cases.C26: Chary's rarity is its strength: precise, legal, and ownable. Yes, some mishear it as 'charity'—but that single phonetic risk is outweighed by perfect semantic fit, zero brand collision, and memorable distinctiveness among generic AI vendors.

cases.C23: Penstock makes the control architecture tangible: a recognised industrial flow regulator, sober and memorable, with clear domains and Companies House availability; its only concern is manageable sound-alike risk.
cases.C20: VeritasGate Labs makes governance explicit: truth plus controlled access, credible for regulated buyers and available across domains; its drawback is familiarity, while the full compound remains distinctive.
cases.C16: Imprimatur signals exactly what CISOs want: formal sign-off before action. The ecclesiastical root reads as gravitas, not gimmick; 'Labs' modernises it, and all key domains are free.
cases.C11: Cautia is short, ownable, and phonetically clean once heard ('caw-tee-a'), evoking caution without being a plain dictionary word. Cautio is a distinct spelling in a different niche (dashcams).
cases.C12: Directly captures human-in-the-loop control for CISOs; 'Labs' cleanly distinguishes it as a broader consultancy-to-product enterprise from single-feature runtime tools like veto.so, with clear UK registry and key domains.
cases.C14: Deliberately formal tone signals serious enterprise governance to regulated buyers; 'Labs' clearly separates it from biometric ID verification apps, securing full domain coverage including .com and clean UK registration.
cases.C29: Archaic, yes—but precision aids memory: a seneschal stewards power only under strict instruction. The word is ownable, domains clear, and the governance metaphor outweighs spelling friction.
cases.C31: Existing Vallum uses are adjacent, not 'Vallum Labs'; vallumlabs.ai/.co.uk are free. The Roman boundary metaphor precisely fits gated AI actions—sober, memorable, and distinct enough for UK company registration.
cases.C26: Chary (CHAIR-ee) names cautious least-privilege posture; charity misread fades once pronounced, and all key domains are free—sober, wry, registrable.
cases.C17: Seneschal (SEN-uh-shul) means delegated, revocable authority—the architecture in one word. Domain scarcity aside, the metaphor is precise, memorable, CISO-sober.
cases.C22: The offshore association actually reinforces the brand: Jersey and Guernsey bailiwicks are famed for strict data-protection regulation, precisely the CISO sensibility needed. The jurisdiction metaphor maps directly to bounded agent authority.
cases.C30: Provost literally means 'put in charge' — the sole officer who delegates bounded authority and demands accountability. That is exactly the architecture of distrust. University admin runs billion-pound regulated enterprises; the title signals governance rigour,
cases.C24: Claustra evokes precise gating—locks open only where authorized—aligning with the distrust architecture. Latin gravitas feels weighty yet modern; claustrophobia risk is mitigated by context and brand storytelling.
cases.C27: Anchorite signals disciplined confinement: agents operate only within sanctioned boundaries, mirroring trusted isolation. The historic nuance adds wit without implying antisocial behavior, differentiating from generic security terms.
cases.C15: It transforms revocation into a security asset. While 'countermanding' sounds disruptive, for a CISO, the absolute power to override autonomous AI is the primary requirement for regulated trust.
cases.C25: Runnymede Labs powerfully embodies constrained AI—power accepting limits, as at Magna Carta. Council/Trust associations are minor; the name's constitutional gravitas and ownable domains (.ai, .io, .co.uk) outweigh them. Memorable, sober, wry without silliness.
